notes.content:
Hey.

I've been steadily working away at v1.3: Upping the Caliber. Its been taking a while because of the unfocused nature of this all-round improvement update. That isn't to say this update won't feature new game changing content, it very much will. 

THE NEW GAME CHANGING CONTENT:
Guns, lots of guns. 9 more new super unique workshop variants in fact. With these additional weapons comes some changes to the game's structure, so you can modify your guns sooner and more frequently while still maintaining the challenge.

notes.title: v1.25
notes.content:
Just a small update while I lay the groundwork for more workshop upgrades, and the systemic changes needed to accommodate them.


[h3]HEAT SYSTEM:[/h3]
The engine heat meter now starts off with a lower maximum, but is now expandable via the two movement speed upgrades. This turns engine heat into an expandable reservoir in which some future weapon mechanics will utilize. Because you can now increase how much heat you make, some heat-dependant systems have been tweaked. 
-THERMOCOUPLE maximum firerate increased.
-Basic core dump no longer empties heat reserve completely.

Experimenting with an SMG rework that utilizes the expanded heat system:
-Accuracy decreases with heat buildup, instead of increasing.
-Shield damage decreased (6 -> 1)
-Firerate takes longer to max-out, but the default firerate is faster.
-Above 66% heat, shots will light enemies on fire while also consuming engine heat.
-THERMOCOUPLE no longer affects it.
-Its workshop upgrade 'PRE-DEPLETED' has been changed from "1 in 5 shots are irradiated" to "Engine heat increases chance to fire irradiated rounds"


[h3]MISC CHANGES:[/h3]
Experimenting with some changes to enemy shooting behaviours:
-Enemy rockets now have significantly less tracking but are much faster.
-Regular speeder bullets do not slow down.
-The triple-shotgunner bullets now start out super slow, but pick up to their top speed quickly.
-Enemies of all kinds become more eager to fire upon first contact as well as repeated contact (if you pop out from behind a rock)

-Gamepad vibration added. This can be adjusted in 'controls' settings.
-Tweaked the Laser Obliterator's pulse-beam attack. With the blue "EMP" attack being removed.
-Increased the firerate of the Plasma Rifles workshop version.
-Increased the damage on the Neutrino Cannon's workshop upgrade (48 -> 54). Its upgraded ammo consumption has also been decreased (875 -> 583).
-THERMAL AMMO CONVERTER upgrade now appears much earlier. It has also been renamed to FRICTION REGENERATOR.
-Removed BULLET FACTORY upgrade.
-When turret rings land, they fire a more deadly attack before entering their normal phase (which now delays its firing for a sec).
-A Weapon truck will now always spawn on the first and last wave of each area. (or every 6th and 9th wave).
-Weapons no longer have a maximum possible spawn wave. I.e a Plasma Rifle can now spawn way later than before.


[h3]FIXES/QOL:[/h3]
-Added button rebinding for keyboard and gamepad. This notably includes new proper glyphs for playstation controllers. Let me know if any keybinds that you'd like to change are missing.
-Added alternate movement style for keyboard users that makes the Sandripper's movement always relative to your aim direction.
-Freshened up the settings menu with better organization and clarity.
-Ammo affected by the UNSTABLE AMMO upgrade now appears as a bundle of bullets.
-Added a core dump cooldown timer so you can't accidentally do it twice.
-Fixed wave spawning issue that caused some later waves to be unusually short while also affecting the gunship spawn rate.
-Fixed an audio related crash.

notes.title: The future of Rippin
notes.content:
Hey!

Thanks for giving the game a shot! Its been a couple weeks since the game hit the digital shelves, so its time to talk about what the heck comes next. 

TL;DR: More gun modifications, and interesting enemies.

[h3]Upgrades[/h3]
Most roguelike-lite-like-esque games have various effects and abilities you combine with your weapons to create more effective, more complex weapons. [i]Most[/i] of Sandripper's weapons come pre-complexified. Which is partly why the upgrades are so focused around improving the capabilities that the weapons start with, instead of substantially altering them. Substantial alterations are left to the workbench upgrades, of which there is currently only 1 for each of the 9 weapons (and some of them barely alter the weapon!). This lack of workbench variety paired with the long wait time to select an upgrade leaves a very noticeable gap in the performance of certain weapons.

So, Instead of making all-new weapons, more sets of workshop upgrades will be created instead. All weapons will (eventually) have 3 dramatically different modifications. Most of which change the use case of the gun completely. Since each workshop upgrade will be substantial enough, they will overwrite each other. These new mods combined with new enemies should give you plenty of synergies and strategies to play with.


[h3]Enemies[/h3]
It's still early days here when it comes to designing future enemies. So I can't give you too many specifics, but I can tell you what I want. 
- A new boss to mark the transition into the late game around wave 30. 
- More enemies that are hard enough to allow for small group fights and 1v1s. 
- Give more enemies some use to the player, like how Cylinders can bonk enemies around.
- Enemies/enemy behaviours that exploit/are exploited by certain weapons.

And something else that doesn't fit into those 2 categories would be more environmental interaction. Like the bombs scattered around the maps. Currently my only idea is to turn the archways into speed boosters, but we'll see what happens.

This will of course take a long while to complete. Especially since the second set of weapon modifications will inevitably throw off my plans for the third set. We'll see how the game evolves over time.

That's all I got for now. Thanks for reading! If you'd like to join in on discussions about the game hop in the discord:  https://discord.gg/SxMJuFfgK8

notes.title: v1.1
notes.content:
The most consistent issue this game has faced since the very beginning of time has been balancing the ammo economy. So to no ones surprise, some weapon combos are too tedious to use! So lets fix that.


[h3]CHANGES TO AMMO POOLS:[/h3]
You start with 3000 rounds (up from 2000) and every weapon now has its own individual magazine. This means firing 2 of the same gun is cheaper, and swapping weapons mid-combat is now a more viable strategy.
-The name of dropped weapons will now change colour depending on how much ammo that weapon currently has.


[h3]AMMO DROP CHANGES:[/h3]
The amount of ammo dropped by enemies has been moved around. Before, all ground enemies would drop the same amount of ammo on death. Now, the amount of ammo dropped is influenced by their rarity/difficulty. So the basic grey speeders wont drop much ammo, while health trucks will drop much more.
-Airships, Cylinders, Gunships, Weapon Trucks etc drop much more ammo on death.
-Ammo pods give 2x ammo


[h3]AMMO UPGRADE CHANGES:[/h3]
The BIG MAG upgrade path now takes longer to fully complete, moving the 2nd and 3rd upgrades farther into the round.
- BIG MAG increases ammo cap to 5000.
- EVEN BIGGER MAG increases ammo cap to 6000
- EXTREMELY LARGE MAG increases ammo cap to 7000
-UNSTABLE AMMO can appear earlier. Only gives double ammo (was triple).
-RECYCLER generally appears a little later.


[h3]WEAPON BALANCING:[/h3]
-GATLING GUN:
- Renamed to "Minigun"
- Since the upgrade "One Eyed Jack" physically cannot increase the fire rate of the Minigun, it now triples the amount of bullets the Minigun fires (which means triple the ammo consumption!!).
- Shield damage reduced back down to 2.
-PLASMA RIFLE:
- Firerate increased slightly
- Ammo consumption increased (100 -> 150)
-SMG:
- Kinetic damage increased (24 -> 26)
- Ammo consumption reduced (100 -> 80)
-SLAM CANNON:
- Bullet range increased
- Ammo consumption reduced (750 -> 660)
- Kinetic damage increased (140 -> 150)
- Firerate decreased
-DRAGON'S RAGE:
- Renamed to simply "Dragon"
- Base firerate increased
- Maximum firerate decreased slightly
-NEUTRINO CANNON:
- Increased the friction of the "shrapnel" particles
- Increased ammo consumption (1,600 -> 1,800)


[h3]MISC CHANGES:[/h3]
-New upgrade ROCKET ROUNDS: + 60% bullet spread, + 30% projectile range.
-Upgrade TUNGSTEN OBLITERATOR reduces firerate by 35% (was 20%).
- The Speedrunner achievement now only requires you to beat wave 5 in 37 seconds or less (up from 35 seconds).
-Starting ammo in challenge mode is now the same as endless.



[h3]FIXES/QOL:[/h3]
-Fixed crashed caused by Cylinder hitting the player.
-Potential fix for game crashing on launch for handheld devices.
-Fixed stat collection issues before wave 11. This bug affected the unlocking of some skins. Sorry about that!
-Fixed workbench upgrade crash if you only had one weapon equipped.
-Fixed ammo counter numbers being incorrect.
-Fixed number display issues with some weapon accuracy stats.
-If you are missing one weapon slot, both firing buttons will now fire your weapon regardless of if ONE EYED JACK is equipped.
-If the game window is not in focus it will now automatically pause.
-Fixed Xs not dissapearing
-WASD can now be used to navigate the Shed menus. The TAB key swaps tabs there as well.
-Fixed a crash caused by audio emitter failure.

notes.title: Out now!
notes.content:
Well, here it is! I hope you all enjoy this thing because I know I've enjoyed working on it! This game was one hell of a journey start to finish, and I'm so glad I actually finished it. Bit off the maximum amount I could chew with this one. Its hard to articulate just how much I've learned making this, the amount of things I'd do differently next time, all that stuff. But one of the biggest reasons why this game got this far in the first place would be the support of all the people that have been testing it since it began. Seriously I don't know how you could play a game that flawed for so long. Check out the credits tab in the main menu to see the wall of martyrs, who combined have probably played a couple thousand hours.

Anyway that's all I'm going to say. Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Test Build 13
notes.content:
Lots of stuff here! The bulk of changes this patch were made with the goal of improving the flow of early to mid rounds by tackling ammo regeneration. Also some late game health attrition changes meant to better reward skill.



[h3]CHANGES:[/h3]
HEALTH:
-Health attrition has received a couple changes. Mid-game Cylinders no longer have a 50/50 health drop chance and will now be a guaranteed health drop up to wave 20 (then they stop dropping health). The Obliterator tank now drops health up to wave 25. The Gunship now takes the role of long-term health guy, dropping health up to wave 35. After that, you're on your own.
-Gunship spawn cooldown has received some adjustment to compliment the health drop change. It can no longer appear multiple times in the same wave, and its cooldown is now based on waves instead of time. For example, shooting it down on wave 8 will stop it from spawning for 3 waves instead of 3 minutes. Its HP scaling has also been made a more aggressive, a proper boss.

WEAPONS:
-The Microwave GIGA BEAM is now cancelable, it no longer locks you into firing until empty. With this change comes a change to the giga beam's radiation capabilities, it now requires you to beam something for longer in order to irradiate it. Beware as this changes the use cases of the giga beam.
-The core replacer ATOMIZER now destroys projectiles and stuns enemies. Its also 2x larger.
-Neutrino Cannon's upgrade now quadruples its damage but consumes all of its ammo upon firing (always requiring a full magazine to fire).
-Annihilator fire rate restored to what it was last patch (a little faster). I didn't really need to change this lol.
-The Minigun's spread is easier to manage.
-The Slam Cannon's spread now has a maximum and is also easier to manage.
-Dragon's Rage rounds damage increased (5 -> 6).
-Dragon's Rage projectiles go a bit further.
-Mag Cannon's railgun damage increased (1,080 -> 1,200)

AMMO ECONOMY CHANGES:
In an effort to make every weapon usable during the early rounds without constantly running out of ammo/feeling forced to pick every ammo upgrade, all weapons now start regenerating ammo sooner but regenerate less of it at a time.
-Ammo regen stats now appear in the shed.
-Neutrino Cannon: Firing cost increased 1,500 -> 1,600.
-Neutrino Cannon: Ammo regen is now 70/sec after 0.5 seconds (was 120/sec after 5 seconds).
-SMG: Regen is now 36/sec after 1 second (was 180/sec after 5 seconds).
-Minigun: Regen is now 60/sec after 1.7 seconds (was 120/sec after 5 seconds).
-Plasma Rifle: Regen is now 60/sec after 2.5 seconds (was 120/sec after 5 seconds).
-Slam Cannon: Regen is now 66/sec after 1 second (was 240/sec after 4 seconds).
-Dragon's Rage: Regen is now 60/sec after 1 second (was 150/sec after 4 seconds).
-Mag Cannon: Regen is now 42/sec after 1 second (was 120/sec after 6 seconds).
-Mag Cannon: Upgraded charge shot now consumes more ammo (1,100 -> 2,000)
-Annihilator: Regen is now 60/sec after 2 seconds (was 120/sec after 4 seconds).
-Microwave Beam: Regen is now 30/sec after 5 seconds (was 30/sec after 7 seconds).
-Microwave Beam regular shots cost more (172 -> 190).

MISC:
-Once all weapons are unlocked, weapon trucks spawn every 3 waves instead of every 5.
-Plasma Rifles and Miniguns stop spawning after the 3rd weapon truck. Other softer-hitting weapons stop spawning but at much later waves, like the Dragon's Rage no longer appears after the 10th weapon truck.
-2 weapon trucks spawn at a time in weekly mode.
-Weapon drop progression is generally more predictable. As in heavier hitting weapons spawn later and later, while cheap weapons stop spawning entirely.
-The amount of enemies and the speed they spawn at has been increased for weekly mode.
-Turret health has been reduced (1200 -> 800).
-Turret orb health reduced (1500 - > 1000).
-LIFESAVER no longer spawns early.
-THE WORKBENCH spawns now work as intended, but has been tweaked for more predictable spacing between upgrades. Selecting it now moves the next workbench spawn up by 15 waves.
-Item drops are more visually defined.
-Core meter "glow" is much smaller, especially at lower resolutions.
-More game tips, now including game FACTS.


[h3]FIXES:[/h3]
-You can no longer take multiple upgrades at once.
-You are now fully invincible during the upgrade screen.
-Item drops no longer disappear during the upgrade screen, same as guns.
-Fixed Shlugoid visuals not lining up correctly.

notes.title: Post-demo progress report
notes.content:
[b]TL;DR[/b] Rambling about what I'm working on.

It has been a few weeks and not much has been shown, but it isn't because nothing has been done. Though truthfully, the amount of issues uncovered by the demo didn't exactly increase my motivation to fix them. So its been a little slower, but we're getting there.

So whats new?
The view camera has been completely overhauled. The "leash" effect when you get close to the edge of the map has been changed to feel way more natural, and less like the camera is being suddenly shoved. Moving the cursor farther from the tank now progressively increases your view distance on a curve, exactly like in Enter the Gungeon. So whipping your mouse to the edge of the screen gives you a big view distance change. While keeping the cursor closer to the middle will not jolt the camera very far. Plus a bunch of other adjustments to camera motion with the goal of being very simple while always looking where you want it to, especially on gamepad.

Gamepad has been a major focus. I didn't realize that this kind of game is intuitively a "controller kind of game" for many people and it was seriously lacking in the design department (me). So the snappy deadzone issue has been resolved and an entirely new joystick input method has been made thanks to [url=https://youtu.be/cYvPQSomwDc?si=FpBs5GkEvi4Gu0vl]Kvelop on youtube[/url]. The previously mentioned camera changes help with letting you see much more than previously. Lastly, I updated gamepad aiming to function with 3 discrete levels of aim assist: 
- Aiming now incorporates a cursor to help with the visualization of a light lock-on style aim assist. 
- The "real" weapon angle also attempts to inch closer to your target. 
- And of course some bullets have magnetism toward enemies.
Increasing the assist level will no longer simply make your bullets more magnetic. Instead it will now increase the maximum angle of the enemy detection cone as well your cursor's stickiness to enemies. Hopefully this feels better!

There was also a total rework to how you equip weapons on the battlefield. The goal with weapon pickups has always been to make it frictionless, something you can do at high speeds. The old system failed at doing that. For some context, the old way to pick up a weapon was to drive within range of it, hold down E (Y on gamepad), and press the fire button of which gun you want to swap out. It was unintuitive, often turning the act of swapping a gun into a disruptive thing. This new system is much simpler. To pick up a weapon, look at the one you want (or hover next to the one you want) and hold down either Q/E (X/B on gamepad) and watch as the weapon magnetically whips toward you and equips itself to either the left or right slot respectively.

A new major feature is also coming... The ability to build your loadout! When you equip a gun for the first time it will be unlocked for use in your shed. Every time you start a new run you can then select which 2 guns you want to use. In the shed you get a nice visual of your tank as well as useful info about each weapon. A secondary use of the shed will be equipping alternate unlockable paint styles for your Sandripper. The goal with letting you play with whatever you want is to encourage experimentation. Theres a lot less risk at wave 1 than at wave 9 when you're less likely to want to use something you aren't familiar with. Of course the biggest factor to a weapon's practicality is how much ammo it consumes, which for a lot of the good ones is quite expensive. So say, equipping 2 Neutrino Cannons at the very start might not be the best decision, but thats entirely up to you!

Speaking of weapons. I've realized recently that by far the most important thing in the whole game is the guns, and thus they should be crazier. So I've been working on doing that. For example, the Mag Cannon (blue charge up shotgun) has been totally changed in order to function like a true shotgun/railgun hybrid. The non-fully charged states are all about slinging big fat wobbly plasma orbs. While the fully charged shot is a super violent light speed projectile that chunks though enemies like butter.

There has also been tons of small fixes to annoying stuff. Like Neutrino rounds getting interrupted by fences, rockets being hard to shoot down, and laser beams hitting you when it really looks like they shouldn't. I've been working on information improvements too so you can make the best decisions possible in the heat of the moment. Like a weapon will now violently flash if you don't have enough ammo to fire it.

Its been busy! Progress has been slower than usual, mostly due to the time it takes to process all the feedback to make it actionable. I still have yet to truly start implementing the new game progression/tutorial hybrid so stay tuned! The best place to keep up to date is in the [url=https://discord.gg/SxMJuFfgK8]Discord[/url], the second best place is on my [url=https://x.com/MackiePalmer_]Twitter[/url]

notes.title: Demo removed
notes.content:
Unfortunately, I severely underestimated the game's complexities, and so threw many people into the fray without enough care put into their first time experience.

The good news for me at least is the game is in fact quite fun once you understand everything and can keep track of 2 double/triple function guns, their ammo, your core heat, while darting around at mach 1... But I need to do a much better job at easing people into that gameplay. 

So the plan is to integrate a much more gradual, more natural tutorial into the core game itself instead of a crappy info dump. As well as polishing up some of the core mechanics and a better sense of game progression. It will take some time to get it all working well enough to truly make the game enjoyable by many more people.

So my apologies to anyone that had a bad experience, and also to those who were actively enjoying the game. The demo will return whenever I can safely say its good enough.

notes.title: Demo PATCH 0.4
notes.content:
Who knew that cramming a whole game into a half-game's worth of time causes gameplay issues! Well I'm here today to attempt to solve some of those issues, as well as streamlining one of the CORE gameplay mechanics.

[h3]Changes to how your engine works:[/h3]
-The only requirement for dumping the core is to have enough fuel. Getting your engine "hot enough" is no longer required.
-The POWER of your core dump INCREASES with engine heat.
-The SMG's firerate is now actually paired to your engine heat
The engine heat bar has been visually overhauled to reflect the changes.

[h3]Demo changes:[/h3]

-Dragons Rage ammo consumption increased +50%
-Neutrino Cannon's projectile speed increased +50%
-Neutrino Cannon's projectile friction increased +25%. AKA less range, more damage
-Roach base damage increased (25 -> 30)
-Roach charge damage increased (150 -> 210)

Misc:
-Camera motion smoothness: BUTTERY
-UI pop up when a controller is connected / disconnected

-Default aim assist increased +10%
-Default volume increased, maximum volume doubled

notes.title: Test Build PATCH 9.2
notes.content:
This patch is meant to smooth out some of the gameplay issues that come with endless mode. The goal of endless mode is to provide an increasingly-hard but increasingly open sandbox for you to play in. Of course there's a limit to how much fun the game can be with its systems, weapons, and enemies. So, the idea of an endless mode is really just a lie because really you should be dead by around the 20 minute mark ːsteamhappyː (but in a fun way).



[h3]HEALTH SCALING:[/h3]
Enemy health steadily increases over the course of a round. By wave 20, most enemies will have 1.5X their base health. By wave 40 they'll have double. Certain enemies scale faster, like the Cylinder, Airship, and Obliterator.

[h3]WEAPON BALANCE:[/h3]
-A fully charged Microwave Beam is no longer heat-cancelable. Spamming the giga beam was way too strong.
-The microwave beam is now impacted by "Expensive Rounds".

-The Neutrino Cannon projectiles have been tweaked a bit. They now have a maximum speed, maximum amount of enemies they can hit, and bounce off plasma shields. However, they now double their velocity and increase their friction with each tick they're inside something. Basically this means you'll get the most bang for you buck if you shove the barrel right into an enemy before firing. 

-SMGs shield damage slightly reduced


[h3]CHANGES:[/h3]
-The upgrade "Expensive Rounds" can now show up again around wave 19.
-New fight for wave 21. As well as changes to the compositions of the waves after 20.
-Cylinders dash attack deals better damage to the enemies it runs over.
-Added a minimum amount of time the Cylinder should be on the ground before it can jump again.
-Cylinder slowly tracks the player as its landing.
-The CUBE is less accurate.
-Easier to see the explosion radius of active falling bombs.
-Increased the ammo refill rate of weapons that you're not currently holding. 


[h3]FIXES:[/h3]

-Your hitbox is back to its previous size (it was accidentally larger).

-You can no longer die to a falling bomb while leaving a map.

notes.title: Test Build 9: ENDLESS EXPANSION
notes.content:
WELCOME TO THE BIGGEST UPDATE. This one pushes the game a huge step closer to completion and I couldn't be happier about it. As always please share your thoughts on whatever you can.


[h3]ENDLESS MODE:[/h3]
The wave cap has been increased to [b]100 WAVES[/b] (it can't be infinite because of reasons). The difficulty spike after wave 10 is a little steeper than before, and continues to ramp up from there. For those who are used to consistently making it to wave 20... [b]YOU WILL NOT. [/b]


[h3]STAGES:[/h3]
Every 5 waves you'll DRIVE to the next battleground! The second stage has a new gameplay element too which is specifically designed for the structure of endless mode. 


[h3]WEAPON OVERHEAT CHANGES/FIXES:[/h3]
- You can now "cancel" the effects of overheating by swapping your guns side. I actually discovered this exploit on my own and decided to make it a feature, I'm quite surprised no one else found it.
- Heat-based weapon pickups will no longer transfer heat from one weapon to the other. So for example you can now swap out a hot Plasminigun for a fresh cold one off the ground.
- Heat UI elements and effects improved, plus the overheating sound now plays on the side of the gun that is overheating.


[h3]ENEMIES:[/h3]
- NEW ENEMY: Bombs.
- NEW ENEMY: Assassin Gunships. Model is a placeholder.
- NEW ENEMY: Turrets.
- "NEW" ENEMY: Regular gun truck.
- New and expanded mini-waves.
- Obliterator? More like oBIGilirator (its bigger).
- Airship has a much higher top speed and will SWOOP by .
- Maximum Shlugoid speeds increased significantly.
- Frag Cannon rounds are now twice the size.


[h3]WEAPONS AND UPGRADES:[/h3]
- ITEM CHANGES: Rapid enemy kills no longer have the chance to drop extra fuel, instead they have the chance to drop extra ammo. Additionally, ammo drop amounts are no longer random, as of now all ammo drops are a specific amount; 5 for a regular kill, 7 if both your guns are low on ammo, plus a 25% chance of an extra 4 from a rapid kill. 

- MICROWAVE BEAM: Now operates with heat. As such, its un-charged ammo usage has been lowered and its fire rate increased to encourage heat-cancelling. It also regenerates its own ammo now, but very slowly and after 7 seconds.
- PLASMA RAIL CANNON: Fully charged shot can now pierce though one enemy. Fully charged shots use a LOT more ammo.

- CHANGED UPGRADES: The "Ripdrive X.0" upgrade series has been dissolved. They're no longer required to equip in a specific order.
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Ripdrive 3.0" is now "Quantum Fuel Tank".
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Ripdrive 4.0" is now "Thermal Ammo Converter".
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Low stress" is now "Plutonium additive", which permanently increases your overall speed.
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Cataclysmic Compression" is now labelled as a core replacer, spews even more core, and requires 2 full cores to use.
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Cleansing Flame" no longer requires you to have "Cataclysmic Compression".
- CHANGED UPGRADE: "Magnetism" is now split into 2 upgrades, the first one doubles your pickup range, the next one triples.
- REMOVED: "Tungsten Obliterator". I don't want players to feel like they have to kneecap their range just for extra damage.
- NEW UPGRADE: "Rifled Barrels": tightens bullet spread and increases bullet speed.
- NEW UPGRADE: "Atomizer Beam" replaces core dump with a giant laser beam. Requires 2 full cores to use.


[h3]HUD:[/h3]
- Score and multiplier HUD elements are a bit smaller now, with their size finally relative to the HUD scale.
- Floating text/damage numbers are now adjustable in video settings (Turn these off for more fps).
- Red vignette flashes on the edges of the screen when taking a hit. Health bar also flashes when on 1 HP.
- Weapon side-swap button reminder now sits in the top left as part of the HUD.
- More visual and audio feedback for being unable to do a core dump.
- The stopwatch/game timer will now only tick up during a wave.


[h3]PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENTS:[/h3]
Things that run a little better:
- Chickens.
- Shlugoids.
- Player tank rendering.
- Basic enemy vehicles (They no longer spam texture swaps).
- HUD rendering.
- Item drops.
- Particles, with better particle settings.
Lowering the particle settings will now sequentially remove different particles. So for example, "Less" will remove your tank's long dust trail and hover effects while "Minimal" will also remove the shorter dust trail.
 

[h3]MISC:[/h3]
- Maximum multiplier drain speed increased significantly, incremental drain speed increased slightly.
- 7 new achievements, with the ones requiring you to reach wave 20 being altered. The upgrade tree one has been removed too.
- Water and bell towers can now be completely destroyed. Still needs proper sprites though.
- The microwave beam now affects the CUBE.
- Bullet impact sounds try their very best not to overlap anymore, which means no more shotgun impact jump scares.
- Fixed some controller menu navigation issues.
- Enemies should no longer get stuck way off screen.
- Shooting down rockets is much easier


[h3]SO WHATS LEFT TO DO?:[/h3]
-Weekly mode of course. Once the tweaking/fixing period for this update cools off it will be my focus.
-A few more upgrades and at least one more unique weapon.
-Stats and achievements menu, aka boring UI stuff.
-Unlockable Sandripper models via the achievements menu.
-Public demo?????

notes.title: Test build 6.0
notes.content:
[h3]The leaderboard has been WIPED.[/h3]

Last week's update brought the largest addition of menus to the game. Some of it needs touching up so that's what this update starts to accomplish. [h3]SCORE SYSTEM CHANGE[/h3]

The reason for lowering this is to reward slow play less. Before, a new player could get a really high score on their first attempt because they were playing [i]relatively[/i] slowly; the multiplier wouldn't decay fast enough for that to have much of an effect. It would then take quite a few attempts to break that high score while playing faster which is a bit backwards.


[h3]--UPGRADE OVERHAUL--[/h3]
-4 upgrades will be displayed at once instead of 2.

notes.title: Test build 5.0
notes.content:
There isn't much in this update that tackle the finer details of game balance. I'm keeping almost all the upgrades unchanged for this one because they will be completely and totally reworked later. With many of them being either flat out removed, or turned into something else. The new score system should shake up your metas a little though. But just know that I am fully aware that many upgrades are not very good lol.

[h3]MENUS:[/h3]
- Main menu and new pause menu added.
- Test build leaderboard available in the main menu.
- Settings menu accessible in game and in the main menu.
- Tutorial available at all times.
- Updated control scheme graphics now show in the "Game" settings tab.

[h3]SCORE SYSTEM 3.0[/h3]
- Multiplier increases when you kill something.
- Rapid kills increase multiplier twice the normal amount.
- Window of time for rapid kills extended.
- Multiplier degradation starts 5 seconds after the start of a wave.
- During boss fights, the multiplier will only decrease if you get hit.
- When hit, the multiplier does not fully reset, instead only decreasing by 20%.
- Rapid kills have a chance for an enemy to drop a second core upon death. 
- Removed near miss points.
- Removed rocket shoot-down points.
- Remove the multiplier UI bar, multiplier is now a decimal number (easier to read at a glance and more compact).

[h3]WEAPONS:[/h3]
- Proper models for all the weapons added in the last update.
- Bullet shield-damage increased (Machine gun/Slam Cannon).
- Machine gun range increased.
- Plasma autogun bullet magnetism decreased.
- Slam Cannon ammo consumption decreased.
- Slam Cannon ammo refill will start after 4 seconds (from 1 second), but rapidly refill ammo instead of slowly.
- Fully charged microwave beam direct-damage decreased slightly.
- Microwave beams no longer set things on fire.

[h3]MISC CHANGES:[/h3]
- Removed the Tank Hunters.
- Irradiated enemies now display their AOE range.
- With the "Cataclysmic Compression" upgrade, core dump length has been slightly reduced.
- Lowered 2nd boss hp a bit (fight took too long imo).
- Ammo will be refilled +50% of the total ammo during upgrade/weapon screens
- Setting the game to 30 fps will only activate when not in the menus. I.e gameplay will be 30 fps but menus will go back to 60 fps. This is a lazy workaround for an issue with how I've set up my menus lol. It be like that sometimes.
- This and all future versions of the game are compiled in a way that will make them run way better. You should feel a performance increase if you were struggling before. 
- There is now proper game stat collection. Like your total kills, most used weapons etc. However the menu to display these stats will come later.
- Camera zooms out a little bit when you boost. Theres also a setting to disable it if you like.

[h3]MISC BUG FIXES:[/h3]
- Items no longer get stuck inside walls and rocks. However now there appear to be issues with them just getting stuck on things lol.
- Cylinder boss can no longer die of status effects while its way up in the air.
- Weapon card text no longer freaks out.

---------------------------

[h3]WHATS NEXT??[/h3]
- TOTAL upgrade rework. Rarities bound to a range of waves, upgrade paths, more interesting upgrades.
- Re-imagined Tank Hunter-esque enemy event.
- Menus to look at personal stats and achievements.
